_help: The one file that defines the crash-test case. Edit it, then run `python3 crashtest.py` (it rebuilds the network if needed). See AGENTS.md / human.md.
area_name: Hôtel de Ville and the southern Marais
_bbox_help: Study area [west, south, east, north] in degrees (WGS84). Keep it small (~1-2 km): bigger areas run slower. Changing it re-downloads the roads from OpenStreetMap.

policy._help: Cars may no longer drive along `street` from its junction with `from` to its junction with `to` (exact OSM street names). The opposite direction stays open. `direction` is only a label for that from->to direction.

always_closed_reason: bus, taxi and bike only since 2020
_always_closed_help: Streets closed to private cars in every scenario, baseline included (e.g. bus-only streets). May be empty.
_residential_help: OSM highway types counted as residential streets (spillover check C1 and mitigation sites).
_demand_help: Random car trips per hour at normal demand; low/high scale it. Too high gridlocks everything, too low shows nothing: tune per area with `python -m crashtest_demo sim <prefix>:FC.M0.DN`.

checks._help: G1 goal: traffic on the closed stretch falls by at least this %. C1 spillover: a residential street rises by more than both. C2 delay: network delay rises by more than both. C3 gridlock is fixed.

_experiment_prefix_help: Experiment IDs look like <prefix>:FC.F1.DN. Any short lowercase word.

evidence.source: Cairns, Hass-Klau & Goodwin, 'Traffic Impact of Highway Capacity Reductions: Assessment of the Evidence' (Landor, 1998)
evidence.claim: When road capacity is removed, part of the traffic does not reappear elsewhere ('traffic evaporation'), but the share varies widely from case to case.

evidence.source: Evaluations of the 2016 closure of the Voie Georges-Pompidou (Paris right-bank lower quays)
evidence.claim: After the lower quays closed, monitoring reported traffic shifting onto nearby parallel routes, including the upper quays, alongside a debate about how much traffic evaporated.

evidence.source: Evaluations of London Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (e.g. Goodman et al., 2021)
evidence.claim: The effect of filtering streets on surrounding roads differs from site to site, so displacement onto other streets has to be checked locally rather than assumed away.
Residential streets have a limited 'environmental capacity': beyond a certain traffic level, living conditions degrade even if the street can physically carry more vehicles.

_evidence_help: Research cards the hypotheses are grounded in (placeholders until live Tavily search). Keep ids E1, E2, ...
